Where in the app:

What it says:

What it should say:

Hi everyone.

I'm excited to be here today to talk about CueCard's *teleprompter*.

[cue smile and pause]

It scrolls your script at _your_ pace, so your eyes stay up and your words stay on track.

[cue pause]

[anchor]

Leave the app and it keeps going in a floating window, right over your camera or your video call.

[cue slow down]

Lost your place? Drag the script back. Running long? Skip ahead to the next anchor.

And the timer turns yellow near the end… and red if you get a _little_ too passionate.

[cue light chuckle]

[anchor]

And these colored words?

[cue emphasize]

Those are your cues. Reminders to smile, pause, or *not panic*. They're never meant to be read out.

[cue pause]

[anchor]

Try it out. I think you'll *love* it.

Hi everyone. Introducing *Cue Cards*. [cue smile]
[separator]
One thought per card. Swipe to the next one when _you're_ ready.
[separator]
The timer at the top keeps you *honest*. [cue light chuckle]
[separator]
Colored words are cues, not lines. [cue emphasize]
[separator]
Thanks for listening. *Questions?*
This intentionally crashes the app to verify Crashlytics reporting.
Teleprompter text can be set from %1$d to %2$d, floating window text from %3$d to %4$d, and editor text from %5$d to %6$d.
Card text can be set from %1$d to %2$d, and editor text from %3$d to %4$d.
Choosing a language for CueCard in the Settings app restarts it in that language.
CueCard follows your phone\'s language, set under System › Languages in the Settings app.
Countdown is the time before the script starts scrolling.
The editor has changes that aren\'t saved. Restoring replaces them with this version.
Swipe right to bring the last card back, or start over.
No account needed. Scripts stay on this device.
Tap the mode name at the top. Teleprompter scrolls your whole script. Cards shows it one card at a time.
Cues are reminders like [cue pause], shown in color and not read out. Type [ or tap Add Cue above the keyboard.
Tap the timer next to Play to set how long you have, when it warns you, and the colors it turns.
Unsaved above Play means there are changes to save. Tap it to save, or tap ⋮ › Save.
Tap ⋮ › Open to see everything you saved. Swipe to rename or delete.
Tap ⋮ › Import to open a text file or a TextPack. It opens in the editor and is kept as a saved note.
Go Back to an Older Version
Every save is a new version. Once a note has more than one, tap the clock at the top to compare changes and restore one.
Keep Notes if the App Is Removed
Notes stay on this device and are deleted with the app. In Saved Notes, choose a notes folder from ⋮ to keep them as files.
Tap ⋮ › Share to send it as text, cues included. A script with images is sent as a TextPack, with its images.
Tap the gear at the top. Each mode keeps its own sizes and cue color.
The buttons fade while the script scrolls so they stay out of the way. Tap the screen to show them again.
Drag the script to go back or skip ahead. It keeps scrolling from where you leave it.
Scroll Speed in Settings sets how many lines pass each minute.
Leave CueCard while the teleprompter is open and your script keeps going in a floating window, handy on video calls. It doesn\'t open while the camera is on.
Know When Time Is Running Out
The timer changes color when you\'re near the end and again once you\'re over time. Pick the colors in the timer.
Each box in the editor is one card. Tap Create New Card to add another.
Swipe, or tap Back and Next. The dots at the top show which card you\'re on.
The time at the top counts down your timer. With no timer set, it counts up from when you started.
Select words and tap B or I above the keyboard. Or type *bold* or _italic_.
That file is larger than 10 MB, so it can\'t be imported.

This script is too long to share.
Enter a title for your note

Add your script here...

Tap Add Cue to drop in a delivery reminder, or type [ to write one yourself.

For example: Welcome everyone [cue smile and pause]
One thought per card.\n\nType [ or tap Add Cue for reminders like [cue pause].

What happened:

What you expected:

Steps to reproduce:
What would you like CueCard to do?\n
Modes, cues, formatting, images and cards
Save, open, import, versions and sharing
Text size, colors, timer and language
Scrolling, recording, mirroring and the floating window
Turning cards, recording and the timer
In the teleprompter\'s timer, set a Countdown to get a few seconds before the script starts scrolling.
Tap the gear at the top, then Language. CueCard is in English, French, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish.
Record a video while the teleprompter is open, even with it floating over the camera, and it shows up here.
CueCard can find the videos you record while the teleprompter is open, and keep each one with its script. They stay in your gallery.
CueCard can\'t see your videos, so it can\'t find the ones you recorded with this script. Allow access in Settings.
CueCard can only see the videos you\'ve chosen, so some takes may be missing.
Tap a take to play it and add tags and notes. Your videos stay in your gallery, and nothing leaves this device.
What worked, and what to change next time
The videos you record with a script

Videos you record in CueCard with a script or deck open are kept as its takes, and so are videos you record in another app while the teleprompter floats over it. Tap the film button next to Play to see them.
Tap a take to play it right in CueCard. Below the video, add tags and notes, like what worked and what to change next time.
Tap the heart on a take. It\'s a favorite in your gallery too.
Swipe left on a take, or play it and tap Delete. It\'s deleted from your gallery too.
Your videos stay in your gallery, and nothing leaves this device.
Allow camera and microphone access in Settings to record videos.
Camera is not ready. Try again.
The camera stopped. Close and reopen the camera to try again.
Camera or microphone unavailable. Try again on a device with a camera.
Sync play and pause on the teleprompter and camera.

Tap the camera next to Help, tapping the screen first if the buttons are hidden. The camera opens in a small window over your script. Tap the red button to record and again to pause, then tap stop to save the video to your gallery. Your script stays out of the video.
Record in Step with the Script

With the camera open, Play starts recording and Pause pauses it. Recording or pausing on the camera plays or pauses the script, and stopping pauses it. Turn off Sync with Teleprompter in Settings to use them separately.

Tap the camera next to Help. The camera opens in a small window over your cards. Tap the red button to record and again to pause, then tap stop to save the video to your gallery. Keep turning cards while you record.
Drag the camera window to any corner. Pinch or double-tap it to change its size, and tap it to hide or show its buttons. Use the buttons to zoom or flip the camera.
An image couldn\'t be added. Try again.
Anchors mark spots in your script, like [anchor]. Type one or tap Add Anchor above the keyboard. In the teleprompter, the buttons at the far left and right jump to the anchor before or after.
Tap the photo above the keyboard to add images from your gallery, or paste one in. Copy an image to paste it into another app.
That file is larger than 100 MB, so it can\'t be imported.
This script couldn\'t be shared. Try again.
Flip the teleprompter and floating window text to read it off a teleprompter\'s glass.
Turn on Flip Horizontally or Flip Vertically under Mirror in Settings to flip the text for a teleprompter\'s glass. The floating window uses the same settings. Both are off by default.
The pointer at the side of the script marks the line to read. Drag it up or down to read where it suits your eyes, and the script lines up with it. Turn off Reading Guide in Settings to hide it.
